##The plan

We can find the area of each trapezoid by multiplying its width by the average of the values of $h(x)$ at the left and right endpoints.

![A trapezoid whose bases are vertical has width b minus a. The left, shorter base has height h of a. The right, taller base has height h of b.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/7fa2b92a61e5ca27a4eb31cd285dee15b33d20ac) 

$\text{area of trapezoid}=(b-a)\left( \dfrac{h(a)+h(b)}{2} \right)$

Then we *sum* all of the areas.

## Area of the trapezoids

Let's find the area of the first trapezoid:

$\begin{align}
\text{Area}_1 &= (3-0) \cdot \dfrac{h(0)+h(3)}{2} \\\\
&= 3\cdot \dfrac{14}{2} \\\\
&=21
\end{align}$

We can repeat the process for the remaining trapezoids.

$\begin{align}
\text{Area}_2 &= (6-3) \dfrac{h(3)+h(6)}{2} \\\\
&= 3\cdot \dfrac{9}{2} \\\\
&=13.5
\end{align}$

$\begin{align}
\text{Area}_3 &= (9-6) \dfrac{h(6)+h(9)}{2} \\\\
&= 3\cdot \dfrac{7}{2} \\\\
&=10.5
\end{align}$
